title: Adaptive workload presets + simulation lens for batching and cache
creator: Sasha Patel
description:
Problem: Users lack an intuitive way to tune batching and KV-caching for diverse production workloads. Existing UX patterns (presets + static recommendations) are hard to map to an app's real cost/latency trade-offs. We need a single console surface that lets engineers pick or author workload-aware presets, preview expected cost/latency/throughput using historical traces or synthetic scenarios, and validate these presets against SLOs and rollout policies.

Goal: Design an 'Adaptive Presets' panel in Redwood Console where a user can: (1) choose an existing preset, (2) create or tweak a preset with explainers for each knob, (3) run a quick simulation using a selected workload (trace or synthetic), (4) see an interactive cost/latency tradeoff visualization, and (5) surface guardrail warnings and rollout compatibility notes (e.g., dedicated pool sizing, quantization side-effects).

Scope: Console UI screens and micro-interactions, copy for explainers, lightweight simulation visualization (client-side charting + server-side simulation hook), prototype flows for design review. Implementation: engineering will connect the simulation API (ENG-2210) and produce sample traces for the prototype.

Out-of-scope: Full autoscaling policy design and backend deployment changes (handled in Dedicated roadmap).

Success metrics: (a) reduce time to first working preset for new users by 40% (measured in onboarding flows), (b) decrease support tickets asking for 'why my latency jumped after enabling cache' by 30% within the release quarter, (c) 15% of teams adopt presets with simulation before rollout in first month after launch.
research_notes: User interviews (n=6) - infra and platform engineers: need fast feedback loop, prefer scenario presets named by workload (chat-burst, search-heavy, low-latency conversational)
Analytics: top 25% of routes have bursty seq-lengths >512 -> batching defaults break frequently
screen_list: Preset editor (knobs: max_batch_size, batching_window_ms, kv_cache_mode, kv_cache_ttl, quantization_profile)
Simulation lens (select trace or synthetic, slider for concurrency, run simulation)
Tradeoff chart (cost per 1M tokens vs median latency, P95 latency overlays)
Guardrail & rollout checks panel (SLO violations, model compatibility, pool sizing warnings)
interaction_notes: Preset editor shows inline explainers on hover with short 'what this changes' and 'risk' bullets
Simulation runs approximate backend estimates; show confidence band and last-run timestamp
If simulation predicts SLO violation, provide one-click actions: reduce load, switch to higher tier preset, postpone rollout
acceptance_criteria: Design reviewed and signed off by PM and two engineers (ENG-2210, ENG-2291)
Prototype demonstrates selecting a preset, editing a knob, running a simulation and seeing updated cost/latency chart
Copy for all explainers written and reviewed for clarity by content UX
Design provides fallback empty states and error states for when traces are unavailable
dependencies_notes: ENG-2210 provides simulation endpoint and sample traces; ENG-2291 will add guardrail rule checks. PM to prioritize sample trace export in the dataset pipeline.
implementation_constraints: Backend returns estimates at 3 confidence levels; frontend must show conservative (p95-safe) default when confidence is low. Current runtime API doesn't return exact per-token cost for quantized variants - we will show 'estimated delta' with link to known limitation in docs.
